title: Epochal Token Drainer for Bandwidth-Smoothing and Async Kernel Hints
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Prefill/decode on heterogeneous multi-GPU clusters exhibits periodic congestion spikes that align poorly with NCCL collective windows and kernel choices. Existing approaches (microbatch steering, rendezvous schedulers) improve average latency but still see tail spikes caused by momentum in token arrivals and suboptimal kernel selection for mixed sequence lengths.

Proposal: Introduce an "epochal token drainer" layer in the runtime scheduler. The drainer groups inflight requests into short time epochs (~5-30ms adjustable) and performs three coordinated actions per epoch: 1) proportional token draining to avoid bursty NCCL collectives, 2) epoch-level kernel hinting that biases kernel selection toward stable, throughput-optimized kernels for that epoch's sequence distribution, and 3) phased NCCL kickoff windows to align peer transfers across pipeline/tensor stages while preserving low-priority low-latency paths. This is a hybrid approach: it intentionally smooths burstiness while respecting latency SLOs for high-priority requests via fast-path bypass.

Goals: reduce 95/99th latency for long-tail workloads, lower NCCL traffic variance, improve GPU kernel throughput by avoiding frequent kernel switches during unstable microbatch composition.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration in the staging runtime with epoch grouping enabled behind a feature flag
95th token latency reduced by >= 15% on our mixed-seq benchmark (seq lengths 16/128/2048) compared to baseline scheduler
NCCL bandwidth variance (per-epoch) reduced by >= 20% in stress tests across heterogeneous node topologies
No regression (>2%) in P50 latency for high-priority fast-path requests when feature flag is enabled
Unit and integration tests for epoch windowing, kernel-hint propagation, and phased NCCL kickoff added and green
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created, initial design sketched with runtime and infra. Spike approved for prototype (estimate 5).
2026-03-03: Prototype epoch bucketer implemented in runtime scheduler; simple draining logic added. Observed 9% reduction in 95th on local 4xA100 with synthetic bursts.
2026-03-05: Integrated kernel-hint metadata on epoch objects. Early experiments show kernel churn reduced by 45% when epoch length is 12ms for mixed-seq trace.

2026-03-07: Added phased NCCL kickoff prototype - aligns all-reduce start times within epoch; saw NCCL traffic variance drop 18% on 8-node heterogeneous testbed. Some tail cases for small sequences regressed, added fast-path bypass plan.
2026-03-08: Design review with runtime and infra teams. Action items: refine bypass policy, add metrics emission for epoch-level stats, and run larger-scale perf sweep on staging cluster.
decisions: Use wall-clock epoch windows (configurable) rather than token-count buckets to better align NCCL windows across peers.
Epoch controller will emit kernel-hint enums (e.g., KERNEL_THROUGHPUT_STABLE, KERNEL_LOW_LATENCY) rather than concrete kernel selectors to keep kernel selection logic decoupled.
Implement an explicit high-priority fast-path that bypasses epoching for requests marked critical to preserve P50 SLA.
Phased NCCL kickoff will schedule transfers inside a small sub-window of the epoch (configurable skew tolerance) to accommodate clock drift and API jitter.
experiments_plan: Phase 0 (spike): microbench on local 4xA100 with synthetic mixed trace (seq16/seq128/seq2048) to validate reductions in kernel churn and NCCL variance.
Phase 1 (staging): run A/B test across 50% of staging capacity against current scheduler for 48h; collect token latencies, NCCL metrics, GPU utilization, kernel selection counts.
Phase 2 (canary): enable on a limited production canary fleet for 24h with detailed telemetry; auto-rollback if 95th latency regresses >10% for any customer shard.
Phase 3 (rollout): gradual ramp to 100% with monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds for P50/P95/P99 regressions.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag: runtime.epochal_drainer.enabled
Start with non-customer-facing debug jobs, then staging A/B, then production canary, follow with full rollout if criteria met
Provide emergency kill switch that disables epoching and reverts to previous scheduler with <30s propagation
Notify on-call and SRE before canary; include playbook entries for observed NCCL stalls or kernel mispredictions
metrics: Per-epoch NCCL bytes sent/received and variance
Kernel-selection flip rate per GPU (switches per second)
Per-request P50/P95/P99 token latency broken down by priority and sequence length bucket
GPU SM utilization and achieved TFLOPS per epoch
Fast-path bypass rate and its latency distribution
